item.title: Hackney Turk shot in restaurant jailed for attack mugshot of Beytullah Gunduz Image source,Met Police Image caption, Beytullah Gunduz has been jailed Published 25 minutes ago An east London gang member who was the intended target of a shooting - in which a nine-year-old girl was hit in the head by a stray bullet - has been jailed for life for plotting a separate gun attack a year later. Beytullah Gunduz, 40, had been sitting in the Evin Restaurant, Dalston, minutes before gunmen opened fire outside in May 2024, leaving the girl with a serious head wound. Gunduz, a senior member of the Hackney Turks gang, has been found guilty of conspiring to murder Onur Guzel, who was shot outside his family's restaurant, also in Dalston, in June 2025. Gunduz refused to attend the Old Bailey on Friday and was sentenced in his absence to a minimum of 20 years. The exterior of a restaurant on a London street, the tape from a police cordon is wound around the crime scene, a chair is slightly tipped up beside a table. Image source,PA Media Image caption, A nine-year-old girl was left with life changing injuries from the shooting at Evin restaurant in Dalston in 2024 The court heard both shootings were part of a violent feud between Gunduz's gang and a rival group, the Tottenham Turks. According to police, the dispute between the Tottenham Turks and Hackney Turks originated from a snooker club fight in 2009. In the first case, Javon Riley, 33, the spotter and getaway driver in the May 2024 attack, was jailed for life last year with a minimum term of 34 years for causing grievous bodily harm with intent to the girl and attempting to murder three men. Guzel, 38, whose family runs the Umut 2000 restaurant, had been caught up in the feud for months before he was shot. In November 2024, his brother was sent a text demanding £100,000, alongside a picture of a gun, jurors heard. In April 2025, gunmen targeting his brother's home went to the wrong address and fired through a neighbour's door. Two days later, five shots were fired at the empty restaurant at 02:00 BST. Guzel told the court both attacks were blamed on the Tottenham Turks. After the family went to the police, the demand rose to £300,000 and his sister-in-law was sent a text warning of another shooting. Before Guzel was shot, the Hackney Turks had also accused his family of paying the Tottenham Turks £100,000 and demanded the same sum for themselves. Guzel said his family had never paid money to any gang. On 20 June 2025, he was on a break from work, talking to his wife on the phone at about 22:00, when he heard a loud bang, then lifted his shirt and saw blood on his lower abdomen. Two police officers gave first aid before he was taken to hospital. In a televised hearing, Judge Mark Lucraft KC said Guzel had been left with injuries that were "permanent" and "irreversible". In his victim impact statement, Guzel said: "The truth is I am no longer the person I was before this happened." Gunduz, who knew Guzel as a regular at the restaurant, denied any involvement. He had previous convictions dating back to 2008, including for possessing an offensive weapon and assaulting a police officer. In mitigation, Miranda Moore KC said Gunduz accepted his "life choices" had left his parents without his support. 00:26 Figure caption, On the evening of the shooting, Riley drove in a stolen car past the restaurant several times to ensure the intended targets were present Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook, external, X, external and Instagram, external. Send your story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk, external Related topics London London violence More on this story Man guilty over role in shooting of girl, 9 Published 18 August 2025 Javon Riley mugshot How a nine-year-old girl got caught up in a gangland shooting Man convicted following Met investigation into Hackney shooting A man has been found guilty of conspiracy to commit murder following a meticulous investigation by Met detectives. The conviction comes as the Met continues to tackle gun crime and disrupt organised criminal networks across London, bringing those responsible for serious violence to justice and making the capital safer. Beytullah Gunduz, 39 (24.06.1986) of Hackney was convicted of attempted murder at the Old Bailey on Friday, 5 June after a jury heard he conspired to shoot a man, aged 37, outside a restaurant in Dalston. The court heard the attack was linked to a dispute involving rival north London organised crime groups. Gunduz conspired to have the victim shot after accusing his family of supporting a rival gang and demanding they pay him £100,000. The shooting has left the man with life-changing injuries and he continues to suffer serious and lasting effects as a result of the attack. Detective Inspector Iain Wallace, who led the investigation, said: “This was a calculated and ruthless attack carried out in a busy public area which could have easily resulted in the loss of life. “Gunduz played a central role in orchestrating this shooting and showed a complete disregard for the safety of both the victim and the wider community. My team utilised CCTV, phone data and forensics to build a compelling case and secure this conviction, despite efforts to evade detection. “Violence linked to organised crime groups has no place on London’s streets. We remain committed to identifying those involved in serious violence and ensuring they are brought before the courts.” The investigation On Friday, 20 June 2025 at 22:53hrs, police were called to reports of a shooting in Crossway, Hackney. Officers, including firearms units, attended with the London Ambulance Service and found a 37‑year‑old man with a gunshot wound. He was taken to hospital and left with life‑changing injuries. Investigators quickly built a strong evidential case using CCTV, phone data and forensic analysis. CCTV captured the shooting and showed a white Kia Niro deliberately slowing, pulling alongside the victim and firing a single close‑range shot before driving away at speed. Just minutes after the attack, officers tracked the car to a nearby street, where it had been set alight. Forensic examination recovered a recovered a bullet from the scene and a burnt petrol can from the vehicle. The gunman was identified, through CCTV, as an associate of Gunduz, who carried out the shooting before fleeing the UK to Turkey shortly afterwards. It is believed he remains in the country. Alongside CCTV, officers conducted detailed phone analysis which proved central to uncovering the conspiracy. This work identified two burner phones used between 17 and 20 June, linking Gunduz to the hitman he hired, with contact around key moments, including in the hours immediately before and after the attack and when the petrol can was purchased. This provided strong evidence of coordination and joint enterprise. When providing his account, the victim revealed that his family had been threatened and extorted by Gunduz on previous occasions. CCTV also revealed a failed shooting attempt on 19 June 2025, when the same white Kia vehicle repeatedly passed the victim’s restaurant before aborting when the man was not present. Through this work, detectives established a clear motive and demonstrated that this attack formed part of a wider, coordinated campaign of violence. He will be sentenced at the same court on Thursday, 2 July.
